task_brief: Day 1 of "Cybersecurity Foundations in a Sandbox" (unit 5, grade 10) is a diagnostic probe on confidentiality integrity and availability. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Write a threat model and defensive hardening plan for a fictional system inside a sandbox; no live or third-party system is probed. Today's work contributes to that by handling confidentiality integrity and availability at the launch and diagnostic stage, against the unit's wider topics of confidentiality integrity and availability, authentication and authorization concepts, encryption and hashing concepts, and recognising and defending against common vulnerability classes. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Before any explanation of confidentiality integrity and availability, record what you already think. Write your current best answer to how confidentiality integrity and availability works, then sketch — in words, boxes, or pseudocode — the steps you believe are involved. Predict one input that would make your sketch fail. Then run or hand-trace your own sketch against two inputs you invent and mark where the prediction held and where it broke. Wrong predictions are the point of this task and cost you nothing; an unrecorded prediction is the only way to lose credit. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about confidentiality integrity and availability, and it belongs to "Cybersecurity Foundations in a Sandbox", which also covers separate topics such as authentication and authorization concepts. Close out with this check before you stop: Name one thing you already understand about confidentiality integrity and availability and one thing you want resolved by the end of the unit. At grade 10 the bar is independent work that justifies its approach against a named alternative you considered and rejected, with the trade-off stated concretely.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.

For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Provide screen-reader-compatible editors, adjustable font and contrast, keyboard-only workflows, and an offline paper-and-trace route for every programming task.
task_accessibility_provisions: Provide a screen-reader-compatible editor, adjustable font size and contrast, and a complete keyboard-only workflow. An offline paper-and-trace route is available for every task here and is scored identically to an on-screen one.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Never use or require a real password, API key, access token, account credential, private message, precise location, or identifiable image; use clearly fictional placeholder values only.
Keep all security work in sandboxed, simulated, or fictional environments; never scan, probe, exploit, or attempt access against real systems, networks, accounts, services, or people.
Use approved sites and tools; do not bypass filters, access controls, licensing, or terms of service.
Treat AI output as a draft to verify and disclose. The tutor may explain concepts, ask diagnostic questions, and help debug, but never silently completes graded project work.

remediation: Reteaching for confidentiality integrity and availability follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for confidentiality integrity and availability, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to confidentiality integrity and availability works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of confidentiality integrity and availability, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking confidentiality integrity and availability mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply confidentiality integrity and availability under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on confidentiality integrity and availability rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
